questions.q: The sternal angle (angle of Louis) lies at the manubriosternal junction and serves as the surface landmark for which costal cartilage?
options: Second costal cartilage
First costal cartilage
Third costal cartilage
Fourth costal cartilage
questions.explain: The sternal angle (manubriosternal joint) lies directly opposite the second costal cartilage, providing the standard anatomical starting point for counting ribs and intercostal spaces on the anterior chest wall.

open.q: Which costal cartilage articulates with the sternum at the level of the sternal angle (angle of Louis)?

questions.q: To which intervertebral disc level does the horizontal plane passing through the sternal angle correspond posteriorly?
options: T4-T5 intervertebral disc
T2-T3 intervertebral disc
T7-T8 intervertebral disc
T10-T11 intervertebral disc
questions.explain: The transthoracic plane passes anteriorly through the sternal angle and posteriorly through the T4-T5 intervertebral disc, marking the boundary between the superior and inferior mediastinum, the tracheal bifurcation, and the start and end of the aortic arch.

open.q: Through which thoracic intervertebral disc level does the horizontal plane of the sternal angle pass posteriorly?

questions.q: In a normal adult, where is the apex beat of the heart palpated on the anterior chest wall?
options: Left 5th intercostal space, just medial to the midclavicular line (about 9 cm from the midline)
Left 4th intercostal space, in the anterior axillary line
Right 5th intercostal space, at the parasternal border
Left 2nd intercostal space, lateral to the sternal margin
questions.explain: The cardiac apex (formed by the inferolateral tip of the left ventricle) produces the apex beat in the left 5th intercostal space roughly 9 cm from the midsternal line, just medial to the midclavicular line.

open.q: State the normal surface location of the cardiac apex beat on the anterior thoracic wall.
accept: left 5th intercostal space medial to midclavicular line

questions.q: Where is the stethoscope placed to best auscultate the aortic valve without interference from overlying bony structures?
options: Right 2nd intercostal space at the sternal margin
Left 2nd intercostal space at the sternal margin
Left 5th intercostal space at the midclavicular line
Left 4th or 5th intercostal space at the lower left sternal border
questions.explain: Although the aortic valve lies behind the left half of the sternum at the 3rd intercostal space, its sound is transmitted upward along the ascending aorta to the right 2nd intercostal space just lateral to the sternum.

open.q: In which intercostal space and on which side of the sternum is the aortic valve best auscultated?

questions.q: Along the midaxillary line, what are the inferior surface margins of the visceral pleura (lung) and the parietal pleura during quiet respiration?
options: Lung at rib 8; parietal pleura at rib 10
Lung at rib 6; parietal pleura at rib 8
Lung at rib 10; parietal pleura at rib 12
Lung at rib 4; parietal pleura at rib 6
questions.explain: The inferior borders of the lung and parietal pleura follow the 6-8-10 and 8-10-12 rule: at the midclavicular line (ribs 6 and 8), midaxillary line (ribs 8 and 10), and scapular line (ribs 10 and 12).

open.q: At the midaxillary line, which ribs mark the inferior border of the lung and the inferior reflection of the parietal pleura respectively?

questions.q: A 26-year-old man requires an emergency tube thoracostomy (chest tube insertion) in the 'safe triangle' of the lateral chest wall. Which anatomical landmark forms the inferior horizontal border of this safe triangle so the diaphragm and liver/spleen are avoided?
options: Horizontal line at the level of the nipple (5th intercostal space)
Costal margin at the 10th rib
Iliac crest
Spine of the scapula
questions.explain: The safe triangle for intercostal drain insertion is bounded anteriorly by the lateral border of pectoralis major, posteriorly by the anterior border of latissimus dorsi, and inferiorly by a horizontal line at the level of the nipple (5th intercostal space).

open.q: Which intercostal space corresponds to the horizontal inferior boundary of the safe triangle for chest tube insertion?

questions.q: The transpyloric plane (Addison plane) lies midway between the jugular (suprasternal) notch and the upper border of the pubic symphysis, passing posteriorly through which vertebral level?
options: Lower border of L1
Body of T12
L3-L4 intervertebral disc
S1 promontory
questions.explain: The transpyloric plane passes through the lower border of the L1 vertebra (roughly a handbreadth below the xiphisternal joint) and intersects the pylorus, fundus of the gallbladder (tip of right 9th costal cartilage), renal hila, and origin of the superior mesenteric artery.

open.q: Through which lumbar vertebral level does the transpyloric plane pass posteriorly?

questions.q: Which surface landmark corresponds to the fundus of the gallbladder on the anterior abdominal wall?
options: Tip of the right 9th costal cartilage where the linea semilunaris meets the costal margin
Midpoint of the inguinal ligament
Umbilicus
Tip of the left 11th rib
questions.explain: The fundus of the gallbladder lies at the intersection of the right lateral vertical (midclavicular/semilunar) line and the right costal margin at the tip of the 9th costal cartilage, which is where Murphy sign is elicited.

open.q: At the tip of which costal cartilage does the fundus of the gallbladder contact the anterior abdominal wall?

questions.q: McBurney point, the surface landmark overlying the base of the vermiform appendix, is located where?
options: One-third of the way along a line from the right anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus
Midway between the anterior superior iliac spine and the pubic symphysis
Two-thirds of the way from the right anterior superior iliac spine to the pubic tubercle
At the intersection of the transpyloric and right midclavicular lines
questions.explain: McBurney point lies at the junction of the lateral one-third and medial two-thirds of the spinoumbilical line drawn from the right anterior superior iliac spine to the umbilicus.

open.q: Define the exact surface location of McBurney point on the anterior abdominal wall.
accept: one-third of the distance from the right ASIS to the umbilicus
junction of lateral one-third and medial two-thirds of spinoumbilical line

questions.q: The supracristal plane connects the highest points of the left and right iliac crests and corresponds to which lumbar vertebral level, commonly used as a landmark for lumbar puncture?
options: L4 spinous process (or L4-L5 interspace)
L1 spinous process
T12 spinous process
S2 spinous process
questions.explain: The supracristal (intercristal/Tuffier) line crosses the L4 spinous process or the L4-L5 intervertebral space, lying safely below the adult conus medullaris (L1-L2) for lumbar puncture.

open.q: Which lumbar spinous process or intervertebral space is intersected by the supracristal plane joining the highest points of the iliac crests?

questions.q: Where is the deep inguinal ring projected onto the surface of the lower anterior abdominal wall?
options: 1.25 cm superior to the midpoint of the inguinal ligament
1.25 cm superolateral to the pubic tubercle
1.25 cm inferior to the midinguinal point
At the anterior superior iliac spine
questions.explain: The deep inguinal ring lies 1.25 cm (half an inch) above the midpoint of the inguinal ligament (halfway between the ASIS and pubic tubercle), whereas the femoral artery pulse is palpated at the midinguinal point (halfway between the ASIS and pubic symphysis).

open.q: Relative to the midpoint of the inguinal ligament, where is the surface projection of the deep inguinal ring located?
accept: 1.25 cm above the midpoint of the inguinal ligament
half an inch above the midpoint of the inguinal ligament
just superior to the midpoint of the inguinal ligament

questions.q: Where is the superficial temporal artery pulse most easily palpated on the side of the head?
options: Immediately anterior to the tragus of the auricle over the posterior root of the zygomatic arch
At the inferior border of the mandible anterior to the masseter
At the medial canthus of the eye
Behind the mastoid process
questions.explain: The superficial temporal artery ascends across the posterior root of the zygomatic process of the temporal bone directly anterior to the tragus of the ear, where its pulsation is readily palpable.

open.q: Where on the lateral aspect of the head is the pulsation of the superficial temporal artery palpated?
accept: in front of the tragus over the zygomatic arch

questions.q: Where is the facial artery pulse palpated as it enters the face?
options: At the inferior border of the mandible immediately anterior to the masseter muscle
Over the bridge of the nose
At the angle of the mandible behind the sternocleidomastoid
Below the middle of the clavicle
questions.explain: The facial artery winds around the inferior margin of the body of the mandible at the anteroinferior angle of the masseter muscle, where it can be compressed against bone to control facial bleeding.

open.q: Along which bony border and anterior to which muscle is the facial artery pulse palpated as it enters the face?
accept: inferior border of mandible anterior to masseter
lower border of mandible in front of masseter

questions.q: At which cervical vertebral level is the arch of the cricoid cartilage palpated in the anterior midline of the neck?
options: C6
C3
C4
T1
questions.explain: The cricoid cartilage lies at the C6 vertebral level, marking the pharyngoesophageal junction, laryngotracheal junction, entry of the inferior thyroid artery, and the site where the common carotid artery can be compressed against Chassaignac tubercle.

open.q: Which cervical vertebra lies directly posterior to the palpable arch of the cricoid cartilage?

questions.q: Where is the brachial artery pulse routinely palpated before applying a stethoscope bell for blood pressure measurement?
options: Medial to the tendon of biceps brachii in the cubital fossa
Lateral to the tendon of biceps brachii
Posterior to the medial epicondyle of the humerus
In the anatomical snuffbox
questions.explain: In the cubital fossa, the brachial artery descends immediately medial to the palpable tendon of the biceps brachii muscle and lateral to the median nerve.

open.q: Relative to the biceps brachii tendon in the cubital fossa, where is the brachial artery pulse palpated?
accept: just medial to biceps brachii tendon

questions.q: At the anterior wrist, the radial artery pulse is palpated immediately lateral to which tendon?
options: Flexor carpi radialis
Palmaris longus
Flexor carpi ulnaris
Extensor pollicis longus
questions.explain: On the distal anterior radius, the radial artery lies superficially between the tendon of brachioradialis laterally and the tendon of flexor carpi radialis medially.

open.q: Lateral to which prominent wrist flexor tendon is the radial artery pulse palpated on the distal anterior forearm?

questions.q: Which peripheral nerve can be rolled and palpated directly behind the medial epicondyle of the humerus?
options: Ulnar nerve
Median nerve
Radial nerve
Musculocutaneous nerve
questions.explain: The ulnar nerve passes superficially through the cubital tunnel posterior to the medial epicondyle of the humerus ('funny bone'), making it readily palpable and susceptible to compression.

open.q: Name the nerve that is palpable in the groove posterior to the medial epicondyle of the humerus.

questions.q: Where is the femoral artery pulse palpated in the groin?
options: At the midinguinal point, midway between the anterior superior iliac spine and the pubic symphysis
Midway between the anterior superior iliac spine and the pubic tubercle
Posterior to the greater trochanter
Immediately medial to the adductor longus tendon
questions.explain: The femoral artery enters the femoral triangle beneath the inguinal ligament at the midinguinal point (halfway between the ASIS and the pubic symphysis), lying medial to the femoral nerve and lateral to the femoral vein.

open.q: Between which two anterior bony pelvic landmarks is the midinguinal point located for palpating the femoral artery pulse?
accept: anterior superior iliac spine and pubic symphysis

questions.q: Behind which ankle landmark is the posterior tibial artery pulse palpated?
options: Midway between the posterior border of the medial malleolus and the calcaneal (Achilles) tendon
Anterior to the lateral malleolus
Over the head of the fibula
Between the first and second metatarsal bases on the dorsum of the foot
questions.explain: The posterior tibial artery curves inferiorly behind the medial malleolus deep to the flexor retinaculum, halfway between the medial malleolus and the medial border of the calcaneal tendon.

open.q: Relative to the medial malleolus and calcaneal tendon, where is the posterior tibial artery pulse palpated?
accept: midway between the medial malleolus and calcaneal tendon

questions.q: Where is the dorsalis pedis artery pulse palpated on the dorsum of the foot?
options: Lateral to the tendon of extensor hallucis longus over the tarsal bones
Medial to the tendon of tibialis anterior
Posterior to the lateral malleolus
Over the tuberosity of the fifth metatarsal
questions.explain: The dorsalis pedis artery (continuation of the anterior tibial artery) runs distally on the dorsum of the foot immediately lateral to the tendon of extensor hallucis longus toward the first intermetatarsal space.

open.q: Lateral to which extensor tendon on the dorsum of the foot is the dorsalis pedis artery pulse palpated?
